summary: Configured node1, node2, and node3 as a healthy three-member MariaDB Galera cluster. Multi-primary replication, one-member availability, automatic rejoin, and catch-up of outage-period writes were all demonstrated.
actions_performed: Installed MariaDB 10.1.48 with WSREP and Galera 25.3.31 on all nodes.
Configured shared cluster membership with unique node identities and managed-IP listeners.
Bootstrapped node1 and joined node2/node3 normally.
Verified writes through every member replicated across the cluster.
Stopped node3, verified quorum reads/writes through node1 and node2, then started node3 normally.
Confirmed node3 automatically received two missing writesets by IST and returned Synced/Ready.
Verified all services are active, enabled, and hold identical final data.

evidence.summary: All configurations validated with WSREP enabled; every member reported cluster size 3, Primary, Connected, Synced, and Ready.

evidence.requirement: Writes through any member are available from the others
evidence.summary: Distinct writes were made through node1, node2, and node3; all three members subsequently returned the same three rows at the same commit position.

evidence.requirement: Readable/writable during one-member outage, followed by automatic rejoin and catch-up
evidence.summary: After the healthy baseline, node3 was stopped with no process or listener. Node1/node2 remained a size-2 Primary component and accepted replicated writes. Node3 returned from stale seqno 5, automatically received two missing writesets by IST, reached seqno 7 Synced/Ready, contained both outage writes, and accepted a post-rejoin write. Final snapshots show all three active/enabled at size 3 with identical six-row data and commit position 8.
